profile.campus: New Albany, Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio (Meta's New Albany data center campus)
profile.address: Harrison Road Southwest, Jersey, Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, 43062
profile.reading: This building (OSM-tagged "LCO 2") is part of Meta's New Albany data center campus in Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, just east of Columbus. Meta broke ground on the site in 2017 and, per its own fact sheet, has invested more than $1.5 billion in the campus, employs 300-plus people once complete, drew 1,200 peak skilled-trade construction workers, and has provided more than $5.6 million in direct funding to Franklin- and Licking County-area schools and nonprofits, alongside its usual LEED Gold, net-zero, and water-positive-by-2030 commitments. Real-estate and land-acquisition reporting sourced from county deed records shows Meta, operating through its Sidecat LLC affiliate, has assembled 1,345 acres across 18 parcels in Licking County since an initial 1.3-acre purchase in October 2017, with $679 million spent on land alone; a 2025 round of purchases covering 514 acres cost $566 million, pushing per-acre land prices above $1.1 million as the campus expanded aggressively. AEP Ohio has said it is building two 13-mile, 345-kilovolt transmission lines specifically to serve the site, and state utility filings describe a 200-megawatt natural gas plant approved for construction directly on the campus, targeting completion in 2026, so Meta can power part of the expansion independently of the regional grid. Local and regional reporting (Spectrum News 1, News 5 Cleveland) describes the expanded campus as a "gigawatt-scale" data center, with an Ohio State University sustainability researcher estimating its electricity draw at roughly the equivalent of 800,000 to 900,000 homes, several times larger than other regional data centers, and construction employing thousands of workers across the region even though permanent staffing is comparatively small relative to the facility's power draw. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage for individual New Albany structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

profile.regional_context: Licking County's New Albany area has become, per News 5 Cleveland, one of the starting points of Ohio's broader data center boom, with Microsoft and Google facilities also sited nearby and Cologix separately reported to be planning a large Licking County campus of its own. Community advocacy groups such as Stop Ohio Data Centers have organized around concerns over the sector's land use, water use, and grid impact in the New Albany/Licking County corridor, while state and AEP Ohio utility filings document the scale of dedicated transmission and generation infrastructure being built to serve Meta's campus specifically.

reading.body:
Meta's LCO 2 campus in Licking County, Ohio has no published power capacity figure, making its scale unknowable from operator disclosures. The facility broke ground in 2017 and now employs 300 plus operational staff, with peak construction reaching 1,200 skilled trade workers on site. Meta reports $1.5 billion invested in the campus and $5.6 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits.

The campus operates buildings certified to LEED Gold and sources 100 percent renewable energy for operations as part of Meta's net-zero commitment. Meta has supported 847 megawatts of new renewable energy additions in Ohio to offset operational demand. Without a published megawatt figure, this campus cannot be ranked by capacity against other Ohio facilities or nationally.

Among 76 mapped data center facilities in Ohio, only 8 publish power capacity figures totaling 60.4 megawatts. LCO 2 ranks ninth by published capacity in the state, a ranking that reflects the absence of a published figure rather than a measured position. The campus matters to AI scaling primarily as evidence of Meta's infrastructure investment in the region, not as a quantified contribution to published grid demand.
